payload.title: fgos decision's supersession guard false-positives on lifecycle enum values:…
payload.description: fgos decision's supersession guard false-positives on lifecycle enum values: SUPERSESSION_PROSE_PATTERN (src/state/store.mjs:1291) matches the bare word 'superseded' anywhere in the decision text, so a decision that merely DEFINES a vocabulary containing that token is refused with exit 4 -- 'decision text reads like a supersession but --relation supersedes:<id> was not declared' (bin/fgos.mjs:2041) -- even though it supersedes nothing. Hit live on 2026-08-25 recording D-tsk28x-15 for tsk-28x, whose text defines a document lifecycle enum 'provisional | active | superseded | retired'; the write had to be reworded to avoid the token, which means the canonical enum name could not be written into the decision log at all. Declaring --relation supersedes:<id> is not a workaround either: there is no prior decision being superseded, so the declaration would be a lie recorded in the log. Recurs for any future decision defining a vocabulary containing superseded/replaces/overrides -- exactly the shape of decisions this project writes when locking a state machine or a status enum. The guard's intent is right (tsk-1lv-1 D2/D8, from bee v2.7.0's audit of 70 prose-only supersessions) and must not be weakened: the fix is to distinguish a supersession NARRATION from a token appearing as a defined value -- e.g. skip matches inside quotes/backticks/enum-list punctuation, or require a sentence-level pattern (subject + verb toward another decision id) rather than a bare word match. Needs a unit test proving both directions: a real prose supersession without --relation is still refused, and an enum-definition text carrying the same word is accepted.

payload.title: Storytelling-material harvesting for fgOS's compound-learn: extract real story material from…
payload.description: Storytelling-material harvesting for fgOS's compound-learn: extract real story material from captures already recorded, per-item at the compound stage, and store it as a pointer catalog rather than writing prose. Split out of tsk-28x by D-tsk28x-12 (2026-08-25) -- tsk-28x keeps the identity axis / topic registry / writer skill; this item owns HARVESTING data, a different job entirely. Deliberately NOT dependent on tsk-28x: the material record lives in .fgos/, not in docs/, so it does not wait on the registry. Settled design carried over from docs/history/compound-learn-artifact-registry/DISCUSSION.md rounds 5-8, do not re-derive: (1) PER-ITEM at compound stage, not a batch scan -- the ranking signal the tsk-1hy probe found (round-count-per-item) is a property of the item itself, and pickNextRetrospectiveItem (src/state/retro-pool.mjs) already receives rawEvents; a batch sweep would be a new remember-to-run step, exactly the shape measured failing at 32% for fgos-indexing. (2) Selection is an ABSOLUTE THRESHOLD, not relative ranking -- carry the known cost: absolute thresholds do not self-calibrate (too low floods, too high yields nothing for a month, and the bar goes stale as items get denser), so it belongs in config with periodic review. (3) A material record is EXTRACTED MATERIAL, not a written article -- named material:draft / extracted_material per D-tsk28x-15; it is a POINTER CATALOG with short verbatim quotes (commit sha, files touched, a few quoted lines) so a person opens the real thing, never a copy of the diff. Content per the product owner: story idea plus real evidence -- struggle/problem to solution, real exchanges, real code, real commits. Known-unfinished work this item must do: (a) item-to-commit linking uses the commit-message convention type(id): -- measured 85 percent coverage over the last 800 commits; do NOT use branch names (fgw/<id> is deleted after merge) and do NOT use branchHeadAtTake (tsk-2zv: recomputed on every reclaim, swallowing earlier commits); must descend the child tree via the parent field because the real code often lives in child items (tsk-19j's code is in tsk-19j-2/-3/-4). (b) The ask vein carries a SECOND boilerplate layer nobody has filtered yet (beyond the four decision-rationale patterns already filtered) -- filter before applying any threshold or the measurement runs on noise. (c) round-count-per-item is a GROUNDED CANDIDATE, not a proven signal: bee could pick signals by AUC because it had a hand-labelled set, fgOS has none -- do not lock it as if measured. (d) The struggle-to-solution shape has NEVER been measured at scale: only 2 examples (tsk-19j, tsk-1ca), and this discussion has twice retracted conclusions drawn from samples that size -- measuring how many items carry BOTH halves, not just the stuck half, may warrant a second read-only probe like tsk-1hy. Evidence base: docs/history/compound-learn-artifact-registry/reports/tsk-1hy-storytelling-material-probe-report.md (tsk-1hy, delivered) -- 10119 events, 314 ask events across ~230 items, 778 singleton rationales after filtering.
